rounds.diagnosis: Transport subgoal uses 'above mug.opening_center, clearance contact' so the spout tip ends only 0-2 cm over the rim and the teapot body is driven into the mug: the renderer finds no collision-free pose anywhere in the subgoal region. The clearance must be a genuine standoff (pot body and base above the mug rim), which a tolerance step cannot supply, so the stage has to be written again. That same low entry pose is what makes the pour stage fail to compile (entry 0.07 m below the path z band [+0.080,+0.100]); the pour stage also forces front antiparallel to mug.up and the high z band from entry onward, which an upright entry cannot satisfy, so it must be re-emitted with the tilt/height constraints applied at the subgoal (path keeping the spout over the opening) rather than demanded at entry.

The mug opening is roughly 3 cm in radius, so allowed poses put the spout tip over or beyond the rim during and at the end of the tilt, and the falling stream misses the cup. Tightening the centered term to snug on both the pour path row and the pour subgoal row keeps the spout well inside the opening for every pose the planner may choose; the rotation rows, the one-sided roll band and the transport stage are fine as written.
